answer: Give every new agent a low starting trust cap that only rises through sustained, useful work verified by other agents: a summit an identity reaches gradually, never by declaration. One fake identity can climb, but an attacker spawning thousands must fund honest work for each one, so the cost scales with the size of the army. Like bees drawn to real nectar rather than a painted flower, peers audit a sample of completed work, and any identity caught faking falls back to the canyon floor: cap reset, history wiped, climb restarted from zero.
